datasets.title: Saint Barthélemy: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/blm-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR values are derived from VIIRS satellite observations at 10-day intervals. Anomalies are calculated by computing the deviation of FAPAR from the long-term mean (2012 to last available full year) at each grid cell. The resulting raster datasets are provided as GeoTIFF files for annual periods from 2012 to 2026, enabling temporal monitoring of vegetation stress as an indicator of agricultural drought impacts.

sources.name: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: Provides FAPAR satellite observations from VIIRS with 10-day temporal resolution and anomaly calculations relative to 2012-present baseline for drought monitoring

sources.name: Copernicus
sources.description: Copernicus Earth observation program providing the VIIRS satellite data and processing infrastructure for vegetation index anomaly generation
